issues.legal_issue: Property inherited in defined shares by heirs governed by the Dayabhaga school is assessed to wealth tax according to each heir’s ownership, rather than as the wealth of a Hindu undivided family merely because the heirs possess it jointly and have not partitioned it.
material_facts: The property belonged individually to the deceased father, who was governed by the Dayabhaga school of Hindu law.
On his death, the property devolved on his heirs, who were governed by the Dayabhaga school and took defined shares in it.
The heirs possessed the property jointly, but their shares were definite and the property had not been partitioned; a partition suit had been filed and a preliminary decree passed.
The Wealth Tax Officer assessed the heirs as a Hindu undivided family, while the High Court held that the property was not assessable jointly in that status.
issues.conclusion: The heirs’ defined shares belonged to them individually and constituted their respective net wealth. The property was therefore assessable according to their individual ownership, not jointly as the wealth of a Hindu undivided family; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 3 and 2(m) of the Wealth-tax Act, wealth tax is charged on the assessee’s net wealth, comprising assets belonging to that assessee. Liability depends on ownership, not mere possession or joint possession. Under the Dayabhaga school, heirs take defined fractional shares when inheritance devolves; the coparcenary has unity of possession but not unity of ownership, and partition particularises ownership rather than first creating the shares. The Court relied on Sreemutty Soorjeemoney Dossee v. Denobundoo Mullick and the Dayabhaga principles described in Colebrooke, Krishna Kamal Bhattacharya, Mulla and Mayne; it explained Commissioner of Wealth-tax, West Bengal v. Gouri Shankar Bhar.

rule.if: wealth_tax_assessment_proceeding and individually_owned_property_inherited and heirs_have_defined_shares and heirs_share_possession

predicates.wealth_tax_assessment_proceeding: The proceeding determines how property is to be assessed for wealth tax.
predicates.individually_owned_property_inherited: A deceased person who owned property individually died, and the property passed to heirs.
predicates.heirs_have_defined_shares: The heirs acquired definite, ascertainable shares in the inherited property.
predicates.heirs_share_possession: The heirs possess the property jointly, whether or not they have partitioned it.
predicates.heirs_assessed_according_to_individual_o: The inherited property is assessed according to the individual ownership of the heirs rather than as the wealth of a single family unit.

issues.definition: When individually owned property passes to heirs with defined shares, joint possession does not prevent assessment according to each heir’s individual ownership.
